key_entities: mutation primitives: add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree
propositions: The existing checker (policy d37e) enforces the mechanism rule (no raw subprocess git) via R1/R2 but misses the protocol rule (mutations via atomic transaction) because primitives are sanctioned at module granularity, allowing callers to compose them into non-atomic sequences outside the lock.

R3 (seam composition rule) must fire on calls to git-adapter mutation primitives made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py), detected via receiver binding (import or dynamic-loader patterns) and limited to the specific primitive set.

Two out-of-transaction sites require durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) cannot route through the atomic seam without sweeping in unintended files and breaking idempotency tests; __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks) is concurrency-safe by using a detached temp index and CAS ref-advance, not by exempting detached-index operations as a blanket rule.

R3 must not fire on non-git-adapter .add()/.commit() calls (e.g., set.add, session.commit) or on read-only exports (commit_email is 'git log -1 --format=%ae', not a mutation), and false-positive floor must verify across src/ and scripts/.
The existing inline marker vocabulary (# raw-git-ok: <reason>) reuses for R3 sanction; a bare marker without reason still fails as marker-without-reason violation.

File-module split (extract pass-lock lifecycle to _pass_lock_lifecycle.py) reduces __main__.py below complexity gates and provides end-to-end verification that R3 applies correctly to relocated code carrying its markers.
